description: Somos un equipo conformado por cinco estudiantes de Ingeniería de Sistemas,apasionados por la tecnología,la innovación y la exploración espacial.Participamos en la NASA Space Apps Challenge con el propósito de poner a prueba nuestros conocimientos,desarrollar soluciones creativas y aportar ideas a los desafíos planteados por la NASA.Nos caracteriza el trabajo en equipo, el pensamiento crítico,la creatividad y el compromiso con el aprendizaje.Buscamos combinar nuestras habilidades en programación
summary: GeoSync is a web platform that helps small and medium farmers decide what to plant and how to care for their crops using NASA open data and artificial intelligence. The user draws a plot on a satellite map; GeoSync computes its area in hectares, queries the NASA POWER API (temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, solar radiation and soil moisture for the last 30 days) and the terrain elevation, and returns three recommended crops with a technical justification, a comparison between options, the ideal soil pH range and a week-by-week planting plan. A second module lets the farmer photograph a coffee, maize or tomato leaf and receive a plant-health diagnosis with a day-by-day recovery plan. Every query is stored in the user's history, and the community can rate and comment on each module. Complex satellite data becomes clear recommendations for the people making decisions in the field, always reminding them to validate with an agronomist.
details: AgroSpace is a free web application that brings NASA data and artificial intelligence to farmers. A farmer outlines their plot on a satellite map, and the application retrieves real-time data—including weather and soil moisture from NASA POWER, as well as elevation from SRTM. Based on this information, an artificial intelligence system recommends the most suitable crops, the ideal soil pH, and a week-by-week planting schedule; it also prevents planting in moorlands (páramos) and protected areas. The platform includes a scanning feature: the farmer takes a photo of a leaf, and a proprietary algorithm identifies damaged areas, while the AI ​​provides a diagnosis and a recovery plan. Additionally, there is a community section where users can rate the tool and suggest improvements. The benefits include reducing crop losses, detecting pests early, and protecting ecosystems—all available in Spanish at no cost. We developed it using Python, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, built on the Django framework and Leaflet, incorporating NASA data, AI via Groq, image analysis using the Pillow library, and deployment on the Render platform. It is an innovative solution that combines satellite data, computer vision, and generative AI, while integrating environmental safeguards and ensuring transparency regarding which model produced each specific result. We designed it with a focus on users with limited technical experience, local climate and crop conditions, sustainability, affordability, and the ethical application of artificial intelligence—serving as a guide for farmers without replacing the role of an agronomist.
